guide.title: Lifting, Moving & Positioning
guide.lead: Back injuries end more EMS careers than anything else. Plan the lift, get enough people and the right device, keep the load close, lift with your legs and never twist. Choose the move by the danger: emergency, urgent or non-urgent.

steps.title: Size it up
steps.text: Patient weight, route, stairs, doors, your equipment's limits.

steps.title: Get help early
steps.text: More people or a lifting team before you need them.

steps.title: One leader
steps.text: Agree the plan; one person counts.

steps.title: Body mechanics
steps.text: Feet shoulder-width apart, back straight, load close, lift with your legs (power lift). Pivot your whole body – never twist your spine.

sections.title: Which move?
rows: Immediate danger: fire, explosion, hazmat, traffic, or you can't reach other patients or do CPR
Drag along the body's long axis: clothes, blanket or shoulder drag. Spinal care is secondary
A life threat that needs moving quickly, e.g. rapid extrication of an unstable patient
Fast, with as much spinal care as possible
Planned transfers: draw sheet, direct ground lift, extremity lift

sections.title: Devices
rows: Always strap the patient: shoulders, chest or waist, legs
Stairs, for patients who can sit
Splits in two; lifts with little movement (hips, spine)
Moulds to the body for spinal and hip injuries
Rated cots and lifts, extra people

sections.title: Positions
rows: Left side, or a wedge under the right hip so she tilts left
Sitting up or on the side

items.label: Trauma assessment
items.sub: Before you move an injured patient

quiz.q: The main cause of career-ending injuries in EMS:

options: Get the patient away from immediate danger fast
Back straight, feet shoulder-width apart, lift with your legs
Legs straight, bend at the waist

quiz.q: Rapid extrication from a vehicle is:
quiz.explanation: Life threat but no immediate scene danger.

quiz.q: Which device splits in two to slide under a patient?
Best device for carrying a seated patient down stairs:

options: Unresponsive patients who are breathing with a pulse
Extra people, bariatric-rated equipment, and lifts if available

quiz.q: Third-trimester pregnant patient lying down: best position?
options: Tilted to her left, e.g. a wedge under the right hip
quiz.explanation: Keeps the uterus off the inferior vena cava.

quiz.q: Most important safety rule for wheeled stretchers:
options: Always secure the patient with straps

quiz.q: You need to turn while carrying a patient. You:
quiz.explanation: Never twist your spine under load.

flashcards.question: Body mechanics rule
flashcards.answer: Lift with your legs, not your back: feet apart, back straight, load close, no twisting.

flashcards.question: When to use an emergency move
flashcards.answer: Immediate danger to patient or rescuer (fire, explosion, hazmat, traffic), or you must reach other patients or start CPR.

flashcards.question: Emergency move example
flashcards.answer: Clothes drag: grab the clothing at the shoulders and pull along the long axis of the body.

flashcards.question: Urgent vs non-urgent moves
flashcards.answer: Urgent: a life threat needing quick movement (rapid extrication). Non-urgent: stable patient, planned transfer.

flashcards.question: Position for respiratory distress
flashcards.answer: Fowler's or semi-Fowler's: sitting up so the diaphragm can work.

flashcards.question: Unresponsive but breathing
flashcards.answer: Recovery position on the side: keeps the airway open and lets fluids drain.

flashcards.question: Pregnancy over 20 weeks
flashcards.answer: Left side, or a wedge under the right hip so she tilts left: keeps the uterus off the inferior vena cava.

flashcards.question: Power lift
flashcards.answer: From a squat with the back straight, feet flat, load close: the legs do the work.

critical.scenario: Rollover: the car is on its roof with thickening smoke from the engine. The confused driver hangs upside down in his belt with a bleeding scalp wound.
critical.question: Which move, and why?

options.t: Emergency move: immediate fire risk – get him out fast along the long axis, spinal care secondary

options.f: Smoke means there may be no time.

options.t: Urgent extrication with full spinal care
options.f: Danger to the scene comes first.

critical.explanation: Support his head as you release the belt so he doesn't fall on his neck.
critical.kpi: Selects an emergency move for immediate scene danger

critical.scenario: 72-year-old with COPD, SpO₂ 82%, 2-word sentences, sitting in a chair at home. You need to move her to the ambulance.
critical.question: Position and move?

options.t: Keep her upright: stair chair or carry chair, then sitting up on the stretcher with continuous oxygen

critical.explanation: Don't make a breathless patient walk.
critical.kpi: Chooses position and device for a patient in respiratory distress

critical.scenario: Second floor, narrow hallway, two flights of stairs: a 115 kg man can't bear weight with a likely hip fracture.
critical.question: Safest plan?

options.t: Pad and support the hip, use a stair chair (or scoop) with enough people, tracks if available; call for help if needed

options.f: Risks a fall and more injury.

options.t: Slide him down on a long board
Let him scoot down the steps

critical.explanation: Pain relief before moving if your protocol allows.
critical.kpi: Plans a safe move for an injured patient on stairs
